Real-Data Examples with QAIDR

Source: vignettes/real-data-analysis.Rmd
real-data-analysis.Rmd

This vignette demonstrates the QAIDR workflow with the cars.int and face.iGAP datasets distributed by the CRAN package dataSDA. It is a package tutorial, not an exact reproduction of the manuscript. The paper’s real-data study uses Face and a 645-station USHCN dataset; its seeded scripts, frozen processed data, and outputs are documented in the GitHub README_REPRODUCIBILITY.md file.

The DR wrappers require symbolicDA; Int-UMAP additionally requires RSDA, umap, and dplyr.

install.packages(c("dataSDA", "symbolicDA", "RSDA", "umap", "dplyr"))

Cars data

cars.int contains 27 car models, four interval-valued variables (Price, Engine Capacity, Top Speed, and Acceleration), and a class variable. The conversion keeps the model names stored in the data’s concept attribute and uses the singleton symbolic sets in class as labels.

library(QAIDR)
data("cars.int", package = "dataSDA")

cars <- interval_data_from_dataSDA(cars.int)
print(cars)
summary(cars)
x_cars <- standardize(cars)

Run the available DR methods and inspect the projected rectangles:

set.seed(20260718)
proj_cars <- run_idr(x_cars)
plot_projections(proj_cars, labels = cars$labels,
                 obs_labels = rownames(cars$centers))

Assess every method–dissimilarity pair at K = 5. The center-only row is an essential comparison: it shows whether interval widths add assessment information beyond the midpoints alone. The default 999 permutations permit finite-sample p-values below 0.05, and pvalues_adj contains the within-family Westfall–Young min-P adjustment.

cars_assessment <- assess_quality(
  x_cars, proj_cars, K = 5,
  perm_test = TRUE, n_perm = 999,
  seed = 20260719, baseline = TRUE
)
print(cars_assessment)
cars_assessment$pvalues_adj

Quality and behavior can also be inspected across neighborhood sizes:

cars_profiles <- k_profiles(x_cars, proj_cars, K_max = 20, baseline = TRUE)
plot_k_profiles(cars_profiles, metric = "Wasserstein")

Face data

face.iGAP contains six interval-valued anthropometric measurements for 27 records. Its row names identify nine people with three replicates each; we derive the person labels by removing the trailing replicate number.

data("face.iGAP", package = "dataSDA")
face_labels <- sub("[[:digit:]]+$", "", rownames(face.iGAP))
face <- interval_data_from_dataSDA(face.iGAP, labels = face_labels)
x_face <- standardize(face)
print(face)
set.seed(20260720)
proj_face <- run_idr(x_face)
plot_projections(proj_face, labels = face$labels,
                 obs_labels = rownames(face$centers))

face_assessment <- assess_quality(
  x_face, proj_face, K = 5,
  perm_test = TRUE, n_perm = 999,
  seed = 20260721, baseline = TRUE
)
print(face_assessment)

face_profiles <- k_profiles(x_face, proj_face, K_max = 20, baseline = TRUE)
plot_k_profiles(face_profiles, metric = "Wasserstein")

Interpreting the indices

Index Type Interpretation
Q_TC Quality Average of trustworthiness and continuity
B_TC Behavior Continuity minus trustworthiness
Q_RE Quality One minus the average relative rank error
B_RE Behavior Intrusion error minus extrusion error
Q_LC Quality Fraction of K-neighbors preserved
B_LC Behavior Bounded local intrusion–extrusion asymmetry

Higher quality values indicate better neighborhood preservation. Behavior values near zero indicate balance; positive values consistently indicate an intrusion-dominated embedding, and negative values indicate an extrusion-dominated embedding. Interpret isolated values together with their K-profiles, tie diagnostics, center-only baseline, and adjusted permutation results.
